title: Trump Fires DOJ Prosecutor to Pursue Retaliatory Case Against Comey
description_short: Trump Fires DOJ Prosecutor to Pursue Retaliatory Case Against Comey
description_medium: Reuters reported that Trump pushed out Eastern District of Virginia U.S. Attorney Erik Siebert after criticizing the lack of charges against political opponents, then installed former personal lawyer Lindsey Halligan to lead the office’s investigations of James Comey and Letitia James. The supplied long account also describes later indictments and a dismissal, but the linked Reuters page returned HTTP 401 and those proceedings could not be confirmed.
description_long: In September 2025, Trump orchestrated the removal of U.S. Attorney Erik Siebert from the Eastern District of Virginia after Siebert, following a five-month investigation, concluded there was not sufficient evidence to charge former FBI Director James Comey. Trump publicly pressured Siebert to resign in an Oval Office address, then fired him when he refused to quit. Trump appointed Lindsey Halligan — a former personal attorney with no prosecutorial experience — as his replacement. Halligan was sworn in on September 22, 2025, and three days later secured a federal grand jury indictment against Comey on charges of making a false statement to Congress and obstructing a congressional proceeding related to 2020 testimony — just before the five-year statute of limitations expired on September 30. Halligan accomplished the indictment despite the full grand jury never reviewing the final indictment text; only the foreperson and one other juror saw it. Federal judges described the investigation as showing a disturbing pattern of profound investigative missteps and potential prosecutorial misconduct. On November 24, 2025, Judge Cameron Currie dismissed the indictment, ruling Halligan had been unlawfully appointed. The DOJ appealed. Comey had famously been fired by Trump during his first term while overseeing the Russia investigation.
organization_tags: U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Virginia

title: King Trump's AI Propaganda Machine: 62 Deepfakes, a Fighter Jet Dropping Feces on Protesters, and False Crowd Photos
description_short: King Trump's AI Propaganda Machine: 62 Deepfakes, a Fighter Jet Dropping Feces on Protesters, and False Crowd Photos
description_medium: WIRED reported that the White House shared synthetic imagery, including an AI video showing Trump in a fighter jet marked “KING TRUMP” dropping feces on fictional No Kings demonstrators in Times Square. The article describes the clip as one example of AI-generated media posted by Trump, alongside depictions of political opponents and other subjects.
description_long: A New York Times review published October 21, 2025 found that Trump had posted AI-generated images or videos at least 62 times to his Truth Social account since late 2022, with approximately half of the AI posts occurring in August and September 2025 alone — a pattern NBC News confirmed independently, identifying dozens of synthetic media posts going to Trump's 10.8 million Truth Social followers and 109.5 million X followers, with individual posts generating tens of millions of views. On October 18, 2025 — the day of nationwide No Kings rallies that organizers said drew nearly 7 million participants — Trump posted an AI video depicting himself wearing a crown in a fighter jet labeled King Trump, dropping what appeared to be feces on protesters in Times Square; guitarist Kenny Loggins issued a statement demanding his Danger Zone recording be removed immediately. The AI propaganda included a deepfake of Rep. Nancy Pelosi using a falsified voice to admit a crime, a July 20, 2025 video falsely showing FBI agents arresting Barack Obama posted at the height of the Epstein file controversy, an image of Trump dressed as pope posted on the White House's official X account in May 2025, and a deepfake promoting medbeds — a fictional cure-all popular in QAnon communities — that was eventually removed. Federal agencies posted AI-generated memes mocking detained migrants, and the White House communications operation embraced synthetic media as official government messaging strategy; Trump shrugged when asked about the pope image, saying I have nothing to do with it before pivoting to praise artificial intelligence as a priority of his administration.
notes: needs_context: the populated long exceeds the requested 300-word maximum and includes a 62-post count, follower figures, and examples not supported by the linked WIRED report reviewed here. WIRED supports a pattern of AI-generated posts and the “KING TRUMP” fighter-jet video, but not every numerical claim in the synopsis. The populated title, short description, and long are retained verbatim. Proposed correction: replace the long with a sourced account within the word limit or provide the NYT/NBC evidence behind the added figures and examples.

title: DOJ Office of Legal Counsel Opinion Rejects ADA/Rehabilitation Act Integration Mandate for State Institutionalization
description_short: DOJ Office of Legal Counsel Opinion Rejects ADA/Rehabilitation Act Integration Mandate for State Institutionalization
description_medium: On June 18, 2026, the Justice Department’s Office of Legal Counsel issued an opinion saying that the ADA and Rehabilitation Act do not require states to provide mental-health services in the most integrated setting or authorize federal agencies to impose such a mandate. The opinion said its reading differed from the common understanding of the Supreme Court’s Olmstead decision; Senator Tammy Duckworth and other Democrats introduced a resolution urging DOJ to withdraw it.
description_long: On June 18, 2026, the Justice Department’s Office of Legal Counsel issued an opinion interpreting Title II of the Americans with Disabilities Act and Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act. It concluded that those statutes do not require states to treat people with mental disabilities in the most integrated setting, and do not authorize executive agencies to impose that requirement. The opinion argued that the Supreme Court’s 1999 Olmstead v. L.C. decision did not establish such a mandate, while acknowledging that its interpretation was out of step with the common understanding of Olmstead in federal courts. On June 25, Senator Tammy Duckworth, joined by Senators Chuck Schumer and Dick Durbin, led Democrats in introducing a resolution urging DOJ to rescind the opinion and reaffirm Olmstead’s disability-rights protections. The opinion is an executive-branch legal interpretation, not a Supreme Court ruling or a new statute. The correction packet gives June 18 as the issuance date, while this record is dated June 22; the descriptions use the opinion’s documented date, but the stored event date still needs upstream correction.
notes: needs_context: the correction packet and official DOJ metadata establish an issuance date of June 18, 2026; the stored date is June 22. The packet also says the opinion’s reading conflicts with the common understanding of Olmstead. Proposed correction: change the event date upstream to June 18; no unsupported page count or claim about a court judgment is included.

title: Peeping at Pageants: Trump Brags About Barging In on Undressed Contestants, Including Minors
description_short: Peeping at Pageants: Trump Brags About Barging In on Undressed Contestants, Including Minors
description_medium: In a recorded 2005 interview, Donald Trump described entering backstage dressing areas at pageants he owned while contestants were changing, saying he was allowed because he owned the pageant. Separately, BuzzFeed News reported that former Miss Teen USA contestants said Trump entered their changing room in 1997; former contestants’ accounts are allegations, distinct from his recorded remarks.
description_long: Donald Trump, who owned the Miss Universe, Miss USA, and Miss Teen USA pageants from 1996 until 2015, repeatedly and publicly boasted about exploiting his ownership status to enter dressing rooms where contestants were naked or changing, telling Howard Stern in a recorded 2005 interview: I'll go backstage before a show and everyone's getting dressed. No men are anywhere, and I'm allowed to go in, because I'm the owner of the pageant and therefore I'm inspecting it. In October 2016, BuzzFeed News reported that at least four contestants in the 1997 Miss Teen USA pageant — in which some girls were as young as 14 — recalled Trump entering their open dressing room while they changed; former Miss Vermont Teen USA Mariah Billado recalled Trump saying, Don't worry, ladies, I've seen it all before. Billado said she told Ivanka Trump, then co-hosting the pageant, who allegedly responded, Yeah, he does that. Tasha Dixon, Miss Arizona 2001, separately told CBS that Trump walked into the Miss USA dressing room during rehearsal when women were topless or naked.
notes: The supplied synopsis distinguishes Trump’s recorded 2005 comments about adult pageants from contestants’ separate accounts of the 1997 Miss Teen USA dressing room. PolitiFact’s linked page returned HTTP 403 in this review; its supplied support note says it rejects a viral misquotation while noting separate former-contestant allegations. Those allegations remain attributed, not stated as a court finding.

title: Sidney Powell Pleads Guilty in Georgia RICO Case
description_short: Sidney Powell Pleads Guilty in Georgia RICO Case
description_medium: On October 19, 2023, attorney Sidney Powell pleaded guilty to six misdemeanor counts of conspiring to interfere with Georgia election duties. Powell agreed to cooperate with prosecutors and testify against co-defendants including Donald Trump. She received six years probation, a ,000 fine, and 100 hours of community service. Powell had been known for promoting the debunked Kraken election fraud conspiracy. Her cooperation gave prosecutors inside knowledge of the fake electors scheme.
